nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox/testing fees and PCI scoping review
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/consultant support
Cloud infra costs for staging/CI environment (3 months)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; estimate is based purely on backlog scope, points-where-given, and rate card.

Unestimated items were sized by analogy to similarly-described estimated items and typical complexity (e.g. RBAC ~ similar to 8-point auth work; legacy migration sized larger due to data volume and risk).
1 story point ~ 6-7 hours of blended engineering effort as a rough conversion baseline, adjusted per role split.

Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) carries the largest share of hours given API, integration, migration and RBAC work; this role is the most heavily loaded and hours allocated (1520h over the engagement) are near the practical ceiling for 1.5 FTE over ~4-5 months - if timeline is compressed, backlog should be trimmed or role headcount increased.
Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) hours (1180h) are sized for a single full-time person across ~4-5 months including design system, dashboard, invoice views, accessibility and responsive work.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) hours (560h) are proportionate to 0.6 FTE capacity; QA coverage is thinner than ideal given the number of features (payments, auth, RBAC) that warrant strong test coverage - flagged as a risk.

DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) hours (320h) cover CI/staging setup, observability and legacy decommission; this is a thin allocation for a 0.4 FTE role and assumes DevOps work is front/back-loaded rather than continuous.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) is treated as High risk/complexity and costed generously due to volume (400k customers, 2M invoice lines) and lack of detail on legacy schema quality.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) assumed to require additional non-labour spend for Stripe sandbox/testing and compliance review.
Some Low-priority items (support ticket submission, admin back-office, usage analytics, contract tests, legacy decommission) are assumed deferrable or reducible in scope to manage total cost.
Estimate assumes no major re-architecture is required and that the Angular frontend and existing API framework are already in place from prior sprints.
input.reasoning: "Total labour hours were allocated across the four staffed roles proportional to their FTE availability and the nature of backlog work: Backend Developer absorbs the largest share due to API, RBAC, payments, migration and GDPR work; Frontend Developer covers UI-heavy items (dashboard, invoice views, design system, accessibility, responsive layout, search UI); QA Engineer hours are set at a level consistent with 0.6 FTE across the full backlog, weighted toward Urgent/High items (auth, payments, RBAC); DevOps Engineer hours cover CI/staging setup, observability and decommissioning, consistent with a 0.4 FTE allocation. Point estimates were used where given (converted at ~6-7 hrs/point blended) and unestimated items were sized by comparison to similar-complexity estimated items, with extra weight for high-risk items like legacy migration and multi-currency. Non-labour costs cover third-party tooling, audits and migration support plus a contingency buffer for the unestimated items and inherent uncertainty given no historical actuals exist. The three scenarios reflect optimistic (features scoped tightly, no major integration friction), most-likely (baseline as estimated), and pessimistic (data migration and payment integration run over, QA and DevOps thin-staffing causes rework) outcomes."

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office), PW-19 (Usage analytics) and PW-23 (Contract tests) to a later phase; all are Low priority and not required for initial customer-facing launch.
reductions.effect: Removes ~260 combined Backend/Frontend/QA hours from current phase; re-added in a future phase if needed.

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer scope on Low-priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) to smoke-testing only rather than full regression coverage.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~100 QA hours; residual risk on rarely-used internal/low-traffic features is acceptable.

reductions.description: Defer PW-14 (Multi-currency support) until post-launch; ship USD-only at launch.
reductions.effect: Removes an estimated 160 Backend + 60 Frontend hours plus associated QA time from current scope.

reductions.description: Use a managed migration service or phased migration (customers first, historical invoice lines in a later batch) for PW-8 instead of a big-bang migration.
reductions.effect: Reduces immediate Backend/DevOps hours and non-labour tooling spend by narrowing the first migration batch.

reductions.description: Reduce non-labour contingency buffer from $15,000 to $8,000 once PW-2, PW-4, PW-6, PW-8, PW-10, PW-14, PW-16, PW-20, PW-22, PW-24 are pointed by the team.
reductions.effect: Lowers built-in uncertainty buffer once real estimates replace analogy-based sizing; increases risk of budget overrun if points come in high.
